One in ihram may not wear a shirt, turban, trousers, cap or saffron-dyed cloth, but one without a lower garment or shoes may wear trousers or trimmed socks.
At Ji'rana, after revelation came upon him, the Prophet told a man in ihram for Umrah to wash off his perfume, remove his cloak and do as in Hajj.
The Prophet fixed where to enter ihram: Dhu'l-Hulaifa for Medina, Juhfa for Syria, Qarn al-Manazil for Najd, Yalamlam for Yemen, Mecca for Meccans; Jabir's report adds Dhat al-'Irq for Iraq.
The Prophet's Talbiya, 'Here I am at Thy service', affirms Allah has no partner and owns praise, grace and sovereignty; Umar and Ibn Umar added words, polytheists added a partner.
The Prophet, after a night and prayer at Dhu'l-Hulaifa, began Talbiya as his camel stood up by its mosque, not at al-Baida', and Ibn Umar modelled four habits on him.
Aisha perfumed the Prophet with her own hand, using the best perfume she could find, before he entered ihram and on leaving it before circling the House.
Aisha pictured perfume and musk glistening in the Prophet's hair parting in ihram, and against Ibn Umar's dislike said she perfumed him, he went round his wives, then entered ihram.
The Prophet was cupped while in ihram, treated sore eyes in ihram with aloes, and Abu Ayyub showed how the Prophet washed his head in ihram.
The ailing Duba'a was told to enter ihram on condition of leaving it where Allah detained her; Asma' bint Umais, having given birth, was told to bathe and enter ihram.
At Dhu'l-Hulaifa the Prophet prayed Zuhr, marked his she-camel on the right of its hump, hung two sandals on its neck, then rode to al-Baida' and pronounced Talbiya.
